content.text: Found it. On line 16, `_NET_RE` is `^Net(\d+)$`: it requires the digits to follow `Net` with no space and is case-sensitive, so `Net 30` and `net 30` fall through to the `TermsError`. I'll allow optional whitespace and ignore case, the same way `_EOM_RE` already does.

content.text:
Fixed. The cause was the `Net N` pattern in `invoice_tools/dates.py`:

- **Before:** `^Net(\d+)$` matched only `Net30` (no space, exact case).
- **After:** `^net\s*(\d+)$` with `re.IGNORECASE`, so `Net 30`, `net30` and `NET  30` all parse.

The CLI (`invoice_tools/cli.py:41`) passes `args.terms` straight to `parse_due_date`, so it picks up the fix with no change. The full suite passes (42 tests).
